tool_summary: Opens a remote shell session or runs a single command on a remote host. An agent invoking ssh extends its effective reach to another machine entirely, which commandant has no visibility into once the session is established.
platform_notes: ssh behavior and flags are consistent across Linux and macOS (OpenSSH is the standard implementation on both).

rules.description: The -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no option (or setting UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null) disables verification that the remote host is who it claims to be, removing protection against connecting to an impostor host via DNS spoofing, ARP spoofing, or a compromised known_hosts entry.

Running ssh with a trailing command executes that command on the remote host non-interactively. The remote command's effects are entirely outside commandant's visibility once the connection is made -- this is functionally similar in opacity to sudo/su, but the boundary crossed is a network host rather than a privilege level.
rules.reversible_note: Reversibility depends entirely on the remote command's effects, which commandant cannot observe or assess since they occur on a different machine.
rules.notes: This rule's raw_pattern is a best-effort heuristic distinguishing 'ssh host command' from a bare interactive session; it may over- or under-match depending on option ordering and is not a full command-line parse.

rules.description: Opens an interactive remote shell session. Everything typed in that session afterward is invisible to commandant, since it is not a separate command invocation commandant assesses -- it exists entirely inside the remote terminal.
